detail_text: Specifically, your firm failed to adequately define the controls to document and evaluate nonconforming product. Your procedure, "Control ofNonconforming Product/Processes Procedure" (QP-009, Rev. L 03/03/2025 and Rev. J, 02/25/2022), requires that all product discovered [redacted] s nonconforming will be documented in a nonconformance log and either on a paper record ( [redacted] ™) or electronically through a [redacted]. Your firm manufactures the SAM Model 9-10000 Sleep Apnea Recorder (K240100, MNR), which is intended to be used as an aid that records airflow, breathing effort, and body position for diagnostic evaluation ofpatients using quantitative and qualitative analysis. Your firm identified [redacted] units since [redacted] of the Class II SAM Model 9-10000 Sleep Apnea Recorder as nonconforming product due to an effort sensor failure and documented them in the nonconformance log with no additional evaluation documented on a [redacted] record or in the [redacted]. Additionally, your firm failed to implement controls to prevent the distribution of potentially nonconforming product and continued to distribute units containing outdated components despite identifying a high failure rate. Based on your firm’s current Risk Management Plan the probability of harm based on the product life cycle should have been identified as probable with a severity level of at minimum, minor; therefore, increasing the risk level to medium. A nonconformance report was not opened until 02/07/2026, over 20 months after the issue was identified, to address all [redacted] units of the SAM Model 9-10000 Sleep Apnea Recorder.

detail_text: The establishment failed to ensure donors are in good health prior to donation. Specifically, donors are not systematically evaluated for pulse regularity at each donation. Specifically, Standard Operating Procedure TOOL-219398, "Donor Screening Job Aid," Version 8.0, states pulse regularity should be checked after being referred to the center medical personnel when initial pulse readings are out of range. Review of donation records for 8 out of 8 donors with out-of-range pulse readings who were referred to the center's physician substitute showed that the [redacted] re-take of the donor's pulse was not performed by the MSS, which would indicate these donors were not screened for an irregular pulse. This donor's pulse was never taken a third time by medical staff. In all cases, donors were not allowed to donate because the pulse was found to be out of range.
